key_insight: The paper introduces Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT), a way to help language agents achieve social goals while using fewer words. In short, it aims to make agents more effective in negotiation and coordination without being unnecessarily verbose.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of balancing successful social interaction with communication efficiency. Language agents often need to explain enough to handle conflicting preferences and constraints, but overly long responses waste time and attention.
method: Use a teacher-assisted training setup to guide agents toward more efficient communication.
Optimize for both social goal attainment and lower communication cost during interactions.
Train agents to convey only the information that meaningfully advances the conversation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to build socially capable agents that are faster, cheaper, and less burdensome to interact with. It is especially relevant for negotiation, coordination, and collaborative assistant systems where concise communication matters.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of verbose vs. communication-efficient agent responses
A flow diagram of Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT)
Trade-off chart showing social success vs. communication cost
Icons for negotiation, coordination, and message length reduction
paper_title: Towards Communication-Efficient Social Intelligence in Language Agents
paper_authors: Linxiao Gong, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Yin Wu, Yili Wang
